specimen_label: Cadaveric prosection of the leg and foot
transcribed_question: Identify the Structure Pinned Green. Identify the Pinned Structure Blue and State its Point of Insertion.

marker.description: Green pin indicating a tendon on the dorsum of the foot.

main_question: Identify the structure indicated by the green pin.
main_explanation: The green pin indicates one of the tendons of the extensor digitorum longus muscle. This muscle is located in the anterior compartment of the leg and its tendons cross the ankle joint to insert into the middle and distal phalanges of the lateral four toes, extending them.

supporting_question.question: Which nerve provides motor innervation to the extensor digitorum longus muscle?
supporting_question.explanation: The extensor digitorum longus muscle is part of the anterior compartment of the leg, which is innervated by the deep fibular nerve (a branch of the common fibular nerve).

true_false.statement: The extensor digitorum longus muscle primarily functions to dorsiflex the ankle and extend the lateral four toes.
true_false.explanation: The extensor digitorum longus is a prime mover for extension of the lateral four toes and also assists in dorsiflexion of the ankle.
